target_customer: Nigerian oil palm smallholders and processors originally, now carbon credit buyers and farmers who use biochar
problem: Palm nut cracking in Nigeria was manual and slow, causing post-harvest loss. The company later turned palm kernel shells into biochar for carbon removal and soil improvement.
business_model: Hardware-enabled food processing, later carbon removal credits and biochar sales
product_category: Agritech processing, then climate tech (biochar carbon removal)

founders.name: Ikenna (Kenna) Nzewi
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Kenna Nzewi as Founder/CEO. Press spells the first name Ikenna.

founders.name: Uzoma Ayogu
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page, which also mentions sanitation and water engineering projects in rural Brazil and Togo.

technical_complexity.rationale: Custom nut-cracking and processing machinery built and operated in Nigeria needs mechanical engineering and field operations. Later biochar plants add industrial process engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary Kraken machines and local processing footprint give some edge. Large processors such as Okomu and Presco have scale, though they use different models per 2021 coverage.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large processors did not copy the small decentralized model in the sources found. They are named only in 2021 articles.

market_need_then: Oil palm processing in Nigeria had heavy post-harvest loss and manual shelling. No dated 2017 evidence was opened beyond a $180K grant after YC reported in later coverage.

branding.domain_note: Uses releaf.africa, and a source lists wereleaf.earth for the biochar arm.

identity.mascot_or_character: Machines named Kraken and Kraken II
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission-led climate and rural development voice

rebrands.why: Not stated. Releaf Earth is described as the climate arm focused on biochar.

brand_strength.rationale: Mostly African tech and climate press coverage of funding and the biochar plant. No brand-focused sources. Name overlaps with other companies called Releaf.

pivots.to: Industrial biochar carbon removal from palm kernel shells
pivots.why: The biochar business grew from the Kraken nut-cracking work and the climate market, per 2025 coverage. A separate spin-off, Biochar Industrial Group, was founded by the same founders and raised $1.5M pre-seed.

outcome_analysis: Releaf raised a 2021 seed and a 2023 pre-Series A, processed over 10,000 tonnes of palm nuts, then moved into industrial biochar with a plant in Cross River State aimed at 40,000 tonnes of CO2 removal by 2030. It is still active and its direction has shifted toward the carbon market.
notes: The 2023 round is labeled pre-Series A by the press but is recorded as other here because the label comes from outlets while the stage list lacks it. A $180K grant after YC and $1.3M from angels (including Eudaimonia Capital) appear in a TechCrunch-derived summary only, so they are not recorded. $4.2M reported by outlets includes the $1.5M grants. Biochar Industrial Group is a separate entity and not recorded as a round. Company site fetch failed on a rate-limited safety check. A YC listing shows the YC slug as releaf, batch listed as W19 on one site conflicts with directory Summer 2017.
